video.title: Fix Your Forehand Over-Rotation | 3 Counter-Rotational Balance Techniques

classification.reason: The coach explains how counter-rotational braking controls hip rotation on the forehand, demonstrates three primary lower-body breaking mechanisms, and provides practice methods.

problem.title_as_question: How do you fix over-rotation and control hip rotation on the forehand?
problem.definition: Players fail to stop or slow their hip rotation through the hitting zone, causing continuous spinning, loss of accuracy, reduced ball speed, and shanking.
prerequisites: loading on the back foot or planting the front foot

quotes.text: counter rotational breaking is a technique that allows you to better control your rotation through your Hitting Zone
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: and if you're not doing it right you're going to hit both slower and less accurately because of that
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: your hip rotation on the beforehand has to be transient which means it starts and stops you don't just twist all the way through contact
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: and that's what stops or at least slows It Through The Hitting Zone which creates that whip effect where the hips stop the Torso flicks through
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: it's the hitting leg kicking back behind the body to break your rotation while you're moving your weight forward into the cor
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: if you watch her hips On Any Given shot the hips fire in but the right leg fires back so she's not just spinning around through the ball
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: so you need to practice driving through that right hip in a way such that it sends the right leg back behind your body and even better sends your entire body forward
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The second kind of counter rotational break we're going to talk about is the left foot kicking up and sometimes kicking across the body
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: now look at that left knee it's rotating out and it stopped rotating out and we can even see in his follow through it rotates back in that's how much force he's using to resist the continuing outward rotation

symptoms.description: Hitting shots with reduced ball speed and lower accuracy.
Spinning out continuously through contact rather than holding a transient hip turn on a linear path.
Front foot or heel lifting off the ground through contact and twisting out.
Shanking the ball wide or flaring the chest wide open through contact.

causes.statement: Twisting all the way through contact instead of making hip rotation transient with a counter-rotational brake.
Failing to press back through the front foot into the ground, letting the foot lift and twist out instead.

angles.summary: Counter-rotational breaking stops or slows the hips through the hitting zone, creating a whip effect where the torso flicks through before relaxing.
Roger Federer hits inside-out forehands employing both hitting-leg kickback and front-leg counter-rotational breaks to achieve the same braking effect.
MLB pitcher Jacob deGrom demonstrates maximum front-leg counter-rotational braking by rotating the front knee back in to resist outward rotation and transfer force linearly.
The coach demonstrates side-by-side shots showing how allowing the front heel to lift causes an over-rotated wide miss, whereas keeping the foot planted through contact maintains control.

solutions.summary: Practice driving through the hitting hip so the back leg kicks behind the body while propelling the entire body forward through the shot.
Allow the unweighted front foot to come off the ground and kick up or across to slow rotation through contact.
Train early swing driving and rotational breaking mechanics with a medicine ball to receive heightened kinesthetic feedback on force production.
Ensure the front foot remains firmly planted on the ground through contact, letting any hop occur only as part of the follow-through.
